item.title: What to Watch in California on Election Day
item.description: Voters are deciding on whether to pass a wealth tax, who will be the state’s next governor and more. Here are five things we’re watching.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Stock
item.media:description: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat, is heavily favored to win Tuesday's race for California governor.

item.title: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject A.I.
item.description: Google is making it easier to restrict its A.I. tools for students. But schools that block A.I. entirely will lose student access to Google’s search engine.
item.dc:creator: Dana Goldstein and Natasha Singer
item.media:description: Google products are ubiquitous in American schools.

item.title: Latinos are now America’s most important swing voters.

item.title: Election Day Could Be a Rainy One in Some Areas
item.description: Researchers have found that bad weather can deter certain voters.
item.dc:creator: Judson Jones
item.media:description: Rain outside a polling location in Cable, Wis., on Election Day 2024. Weather can be an uncontrollable and slightly unpredictable factor in elections.

item.title: How to Follow The New York Times’s 2026 Midterm Election Results and Coverage

item.title: Trump Effort to Prove Rampant Noncitizen Voting Leads to Few Charges So Far
item.description: Just 236 people have been charged with voting-fraud-related offenses by the Trump administration, despite its unsubstantiated claims that fraud is widespread.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ballots in Los Angeles County in November 2024. The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected a federal effort to set aside midterm ballots this year from 20,000 people in California who the Trump administration suspects are “likely noncitizens.”

item.title: Are the Polls Right About Democrats?
item.description: Nate Cohn, our chief political analyst, explains how polling has fared in the Trump era and whether we should trust this year’s midterm polls that are favorable to Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Nate Cohn, Laura Bult, June Kim and Edward Vega

item.title: Supreme Court to Hear Catholic Schools’ Challenge to Colorado Aid Rules
item.description: The Supreme Court considers whether Catholic preschools in Colorado that decline to enroll families with gay and transgender parents can participate in a state program.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow

item.media:description: The St. Mary Catholic Parish preschool in Littleton, Colo. The parish is part of a lawsuit against the State of Colorado that the Supreme Court will hear on Tuesday.

item.title: 6 Themes to Watch for in the Midterms Elections Results
item.description: Republicans are bracing for losses amid a backlash to the president’s economic leadership and the Iran war. Whether that means giving up control of the Senate is Tuesday’s biggest question.

item.media:description: Voters in Anchorage on Sunday. A Democratic plan to recruit a spoiler candidate into the state’s Senate race has angered Republicans.

item.title: What’s at Stake in Today’s Elections
item.description: Though President Trump’s name is not on the ballot, voters are weighing the effects of his agenda in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Lisa Lerer, a national political reporter for The New York Times, describes how three crucial issues are affecting their decisions.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer, Gilad Thaler, Jon Miller, James Surdam, Nikolay Nikolov and Rafaela Balster

item.title: What to Watch in Michigan

item.title: Flouting Consumer Law, Insurers Refuse to Pay Medical Bills for Emergency Care
